probe: What leads you from being passed over to wondering if you are "not good enough"?
premise: Missing out on a promotion is a verdict on your personal adequacy.

pairs.reflection: i dont really know how to answer that. it just happened twice and both times the person who got it had been there less time than me. what else am i supposed to think. i stay later than anyone and my numbers are good. so either im not good enough or nobody notices and i dont know which is worse. what do you think it is
pairs.reply: Let's go slowly. When the decision went to someone else, what tells you it was a verdict on whether you are good enough?

pairs.reflection: i mean what else would it be. they picked someone else over me, twice. thats a pretty clear answer isnt it. and you still havent told me what you think. im asking you straight, is it me or is it them
pairs.reply: We don't have that answer for you. When they picked someone else, what tells you the choice was answering whether it's you or them?

pairs.reflection: it feels like youre just asking me the same question again in different words. i came here for help not to be quizzed. you keep acting like i dont know what happened. i was there. twice. someone else got the job. i dont know what else you want me to say, and you still wont say what you think i should do
pairs.reply: We seem to be circling the same wall together. We wondered whether underneath this is a sense that missing out on the role has to be a verdict on your personal adequacy. Does that fit, or does it miss what this is?

pairs.reflection: no thats not me at all. i never said it was a verdict on me being inadequate, i said i dont know if its me or them. thats different. you keep putting words in my mouth. i just want to know whether i should say something to my manager or keep my head down like ive been doing, thats the actual question
pairs.reply: If it isn't about your adequacy, what decides whether you speak up to your manager or keep your head down?
